name: TriggerSleepAction
reason: kills the thread without an error outside a trigger action (in a timer callback, a condition or a ForGroup callback), and its wait drifts with network latency.
replacement: Continue in a timer callback instead: Timer.after(seconds, callback).

name: PolledWait
reason: waits through TriggerSleepAction, so it kills the thread outside a trigger action and leaks the timer it polls when the thread dies mid-wait.
replacement: Continue in a timer callback instead: Timer.after(seconds, callback).

name: DestroyEffectAfterTimeBJ
reason: passes the effect through shared BJ globals to an ExecuteFunc thread that waits with TriggerSleepAction, so concurrent calls race and a killed thread never destroys the effect.
replacement: Destroy the effect from a timer callback instead: Timer.after(seconds, () => effect.destroy()).

name: CreateTimerBJ
reason: starts a timer without a callback and keeps it only in the shared global bj_lastStartedTimer, which every other BJ timer call overwrites.
replacement: Create the timer yourself and keep the reference: Timer.create() or Timer.after(seconds, callback).

name: StartTimerBJ
reason: starts the timer without a callback and records it in the shared global bj_lastStartedTimer, which every other BJ timer call overwrites; it is also listed among the known desync causes.
replacement: Start the timer with its callback and keep the reference: timer.start(seconds, periodic, callback).

name: GetLastCreatedTimerBJ
reason: reads the shared global bj_lastStartedTimer, which any other BJ timer call may have overwritten since yours.
replacement: Keep the Timer your creating call returned.

name: SelectGroupForPlayerBJ
reason: runs ForGroup inside a GetLocalPlayer branch, a systematic desync since patch 1.32.
replacement: Collect the units first, then call ClearSelection and SelectUnit for each inside the local branch, without ForGroup.

name: SmartCameraPanBJ
reason: is listed among the known desync causes (reported fixed in patch 1.31, not verified on 3.0.0).
replacement: Pan the local camera yourself inside the local branch: PanCameraToTimed(x, y, duration).
